subject.title: [Feature]: Subagent session reuse for expert agents (avoid new session per spawn)

question: Should OpenClaw add a general native subagent reuse contract, limit this to a Teams session-binding adapter, or keep native `sessions_spawn` isolated by default?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the safe fix shape changes session-state/API semantics and could affect isolation, concurrency, cleanup, and channel routing.

options.title: Design native reuse contract
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in native reuse/pooling API with scope, TTL, locking, cleanup, and regression tests before implementation.

options.title: Limit to Teams binding
options.body: Implement only a Teams session-binding adapter so `thread: true`/`mode: "session"` can persist in Teams without changing non-thread native spawn behavior.

options.title: Keep fresh native sessions
options.body: Leave native spawns isolated and document `sessions_send` or thread-bound channels as the supported persistence paths.

recommendation.title: Design native reuse contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in native reuse/pooling API with scope, TTL, locking, cleanup, and regression tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to steipete as the strongest owner for the subagent spawn/session-binding API boundary and product tradeoff.
